extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent applicants, and patent office adjudicators (JPO practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, standards and procedural criteria governing examination, appeals, oppositions, trials for invalidation and correction, and Hantei advisory opinions before the Japan Patent Office (TAD). Useful for practitioners handling JPO administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPO role and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The JPO is the administrative agency responsible for administration of industrial property laws, headed by a commissioner and including examination departments and a Trial and Appeal Department (TAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes organization into examination departments and a TAD that conducts trials and appeals; identifies four technical fields for examiners and the TAD's 38 boards (33 for patents/utility models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examinations conducted in accordance with Examination Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Examinations are conducted in accordance with the Examination Guidelines for Patent and Utility Model in Japan prepared by the JPO to ensure consistent decisions and transparent processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines address principles/procedures of examination, requirements for patentability, descriptions and claims, priority, foreign-language applications, and patent term extension; an English version is available on the JPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to refuse non-compliant applications and applicant notice opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner must refuse a patent application if it does not comply with the Patent Act, but before reaching that decision must notify the applicant of the grounds for refusal and give them an opportunity to submit a written opinion within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural duty ensures applicants can respond prior to refusal; ties examination refusals to statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality check for trial/appeal filings
rubrics_metrics.description: When requests for a trial or appeal are filed with the TAD, trial clerks first conduct a formality check to assess whether the purpose and reason for the request is stated, fees paid, and necessary documents (e.g., power of attorney) are attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After formality check, cases are sent to the specialized TAD board in charge; failure on formality grounds results in notification and an opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panels and panel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals and trials are conducted by a panel consisting of three or five administrative patent judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels may include administrative patent judges with specialized technical expertise; five-judge panels are used in certain cases (example reference to published five-judge decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex officio proceedings authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Panels may conduct ex officio proceedings, allowing them to investigate facts and examine evidence on their own authority, including grounds not pleaded by parties (subject to limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex officio examination is permitted because trials serve broader public interests; when ex officio proceedings are invoked, panels must provide notice of reasons and allow formal responses. Panels cannot examine any claim not claimed by a demandant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual for Trial and Appeal Proceedings as binding procedural guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative patent judges conduct proceedings in accordance with the Manual for Trial and Appeal Proceedings, the Examination Guidelines, court decisions and other trial and appeal decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual aims to ensure uniform understanding, consistent and transparent procedures, and fair and accurate decisions; parts available in English on the JPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence submission and proof requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may submit evidence up until the conclusion of a trial or appeal; evidence and its relationship to the facts to be proved must be identified in writing, and foreign-language documents require translations of the relevant parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence (patent gazettes, journals, catalogs, blueprints, order forms, delivery slips) is common; witness examination is possible in invalidation trials; expert opinion, inspection of evidence, and videoconference testimony may be used; panels may preserve evidence per civil procedure rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel must specify the claimed invention based on the description of the claims and construe the claims by referring to the description, drawings and common general knowledge in the technical field at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims and description/drawings do not correspond, the panel must not specify the claimed invention based only on the description or drawings; matters described in the claims must always be taken into consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal against examiner's decision of refusal — timing and form
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may file an appeal against an examiner’s decision of refusal within three months (four months for parties residing outside Japan) from service of a certified copy of the examiner’s decision; if prevented for reasons beyond control, a shortened grace period applies (14 days or two months abroad) but no later than six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals are ex parte documentary proceedings initiated by an appellant (demandant) and conducted by a panel of administrative patent judges; panels may conduct ex officio investigations if decision was inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to grant — who may file and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may file an opposition to the grant of a patent; oppositions do not require an interest, but anonymous oppositions are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oppositions must be filed within six months from the publication of a gazette containing the patent; if a patent has multiple claims, an opposition may be filed for each claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition — scope of examination and panel practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel will examine only the claims to which an opposition is filed and will conduct examination based on the reasons and evidence pleaded by the demandant, although it may examine unpleaded reasons via ex officio proceedings under certain considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to invoke ex officio proceedings must take into account public interest, purpose of the process, delay, and whether ex officio examination will produce a more accurate determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition — notification, correction opportunity and finality
rubrics_metrics.description: If a panel intends to render a revocation decision in opposition proceedings, the judge must notify the patentee and intervenors of the grounds and provide an opportunity to submit a written opinion within a reasonable period; the patentee may request correction within that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent is revoked and decision becomes final and binding, the patent is deemed never to have existed; if the panel maintains the patent and decision becomes final, parties cannot bring a revocation action against that decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for correction — permissible corrections (Article 126(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections that may be requested in a trial for correction are limited to: restriction of the claims, correction of errors or mistranslations, clarification of any ambiguous statement, or rewriting a claim that cites the preceding claim so that it does not cite the preceding claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correction is usually preventive to guard against invalidation or to clarify ambiguity; requests for correction cannot be filed while an invalidation trial is pending and until its final resolution, except at prescribed times; a correction request may not add new matter or change gist of a request without prohibition; chief administrative patent judge must notify reasons for rejection and provide opportunity to submit written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for correction — procedural consequences of approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If a decision to allow a correction becomes final and binding, filing, publication, examiner’s decision to grant, and registration are deemed to have been made based on the corrected claims, descriptions or drawings with retroactive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for correction may be filed even after forfeiture of the patent right but not after revocation or invalidation; if amendment changes the gist of the request it will not be adopted and proceedings conclude with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for invalidation — inter partes requirement and interested person standing
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials for invalidation are inter partes proceedings involving a demandant (interested person) and the demandee (patentee); only an 'interested person' may file a request for invalidation, and whether a person is interested is determined case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of interested persons include those sued for infringement, manufacturers of the same product, or persons claiming a legitimate right to obtain a patent (co-owners, transferees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial for invalidation — grounds for invalidation (Article 123(1) exhaustive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons for invalidation are limited to statutory reasons under Article 123(1)(i)–(viii), including (inter alia): patents granted on amendments beyond the original disclosure; grants in violation of Articles on enjoyment of rights, conditions for patentability, unpatentable inventions, joint applications; grants in violation of a treaty; failure to comply with requirements for statements of detailed explanation/claims; foreign-language application matters exceeding scope; grants to persons without right; post-grant disqualifying events; improper corrections in violation of Article 126 provisos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No other reasons outside statutory provisions constitute grounds for invalidation; requests may be filed claim-by-claim where multiple claims are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee written reply and request for correction in invalidation trials
rubrics_metrics.description: After a demandant files for invalidation, a patentee may submit written replies and file a request for correction to protect patent rights; the request must identify the purpose and must not add new matter or substantially expand/change claim scope and must fulfill independent patentability requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time limits apply: e.g., request for correction generally must be filed within the time limit for submitting a written reply after receiving duplicates of the written request or after advance notice of a trial decision; corrections requested may include restriction of claims and clarification of ambiguous statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to demandant's request and limits to changing gist
rubrics_metrics.description: Demandants may not, in principle, amend the request for a trial to change the gist of the reasons (e.g., changing the ground from inventive step to clarity), to avoid unreasonable delay; amendments may be allowed if no risk of unreasonable delay and amendment is in response to patentee's request for correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule balances flexibility with procedural efficiency; panels can control amendments to avoid delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral proceedings practice for invalidation trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Trials for invalidation are generally conducted as oral proceedings where panel and parties communicate to understand and resolve disputed issues, including technical matters; online oral proceedings are possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels send a written 'notice of proceedings matters' beforehand containing preliminary view, issues in dispute, and requests for technical explanations; parties must submit an 'oral proceedings statement brief' in advance to clarify arguments and evidence; oral proceedings can include witness examination and address ex officio issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice of trial decision procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: When a panel is ready to make a trial decision following oral proceedings (e.g., when a reason for the request is approved or a request for correction is not approved), the panel will provide parties with an advance notice of the trial decision that contains the same matters and level of detail as the final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice lets patentees request correction or amendment before finalizing; exceptions where advance notice is not provided include when patentee declines advance notice, patentee does not file request for correction and all claims are valid, or all requested corrections are approved and claims valid; procedure prevents 'catch-ball' remands between JPO and IP High Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and reasoning in trial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The trial decision must include the issues in dispute and determinations, deciding all the reasons for invalidation (including ex officio reasons), present conclusions and specific reasons, and explain refusal of amendments that change gist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties dissatisfied with trial decisions may file revocation actions with the IP High Court; trial decisions determine the degree to which peripheral reasons for invalidation are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hantei (advisory opinion) system — nature and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Hantei is a nonbinding official advisory opinion on the technical scope of a patented invention provided by the TAD; it is an administrative service, neither legally binding nor appealable; no legal interest is required but a benefit must be shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either patentee or non-patentee may request Hantei to determine whether a product or planned technology falls within the technical scope of a patented invention; process requires written request and gives demandee opportunity to file written answer; Hantei examines technical scope including the doctrine of equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hantei for standard-essential patents (SEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A specialized Hantei process for SEPs (implemented 2018) facilitates license negotiations by improving transparency of a patent’s actual essentiality; demandants must identify a 'virtual object' from a technical standard for comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A panel of three administrative patent judges compares the patented invention and the identified virtual object and assesses whether the virtual object falls within the technical scope; if so, the patent is determined to be a standard-essential patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits and procedural timelines across processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Various strict timing rules apply: appeals against refusal (3 months domestic, 4 months foreign; grace rules if prevented), opposition to grant (within six months of gazette publication), statutory time limits for correction requests and other deadlines under the Patent Act and Manual for Proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple specific Patent Act articles referenced for other time limits (arts 134, 153, 164-2 etc.); practitioners must track jurisdiction-specific deadlines carefully to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention rights in opposition proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person that has a right or an interest in the patent may intervene in opposition proceedings to assist the patentee until a decision is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervention is permitted in oppositions (Patent Act art.119(1)); by contrast, in some other proceedings (e.g., trial for correction) intervention is not permitted as provided by statute.
